suggestions: pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
convert an IN subquery to a semi-join (multiple times)
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
optimized_sql:
select cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, count(*) cnt1, cd_purchase_estimate, count(*) cnt2, cd_credit_rating, count(*) cnt3
from customer c
join customer_address ca on c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
join customer_demographics on customer_demographics.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
where ca_state in ('IL','TX','ME')
and exists (
    select * from store_sales
    join date_dim on store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
    where c.c_customer_sk = store_sales.ss_customer_sk
      and date_dim.d_year = 2002
      and date_dim.d_moy between 1 and 1+2
)
and (
    not exists (
        select * from web_sales
        join date_dim on web_sales.ws_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
        where c.c_customer_sk = web_sales.ws_bill_customer_sk
          and date_dim.d_year = 2002
          and date_dim.d_moy between 1 and 1+2
    )
    and not exists (
        select * from catalog_sales
        join date_dim on catalog_sales.cs_sold_date_sk = date_dim.d_date_sk
        where c.c_customer_sk = catalog_sales.cs_ship_customer_sk
          and date_dim.d_year = 2002
          and date_dim.d_moy between 1 and 1+2
    )
)
group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
order by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, cd_purchase_estimate, cd_credit_rating
limit 100
